name: stage-raster-polygon
summary: a generic stage of the stage program: closed polygons from a shape file rasterised to a coverage matte with the coverage-raster crate and carried in the frame; a published method under explicit configuration, not compared with any product

binaries.name: mocha-stage
binaries.arguments: apply raster-polygon --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --fps N[/D] [--frames N] [--describe] [--param K=V]... [--layer shape=PATH] [--layer keys=PATH]
binaries.stdin: whole raw frames; not read with --describe
binaries.stdout: one frame per input frame, of the size of the input; with --describe one line of JSON
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

frame_contract: frames/2 raw frames on standard input and output: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame
computes: per frame every point of the polygons is moved by offset_x and offset_y, coverage_raster::rasterise_buffer gives one coverage value per pixel on a target of the frame size with its origin at 0, 0, apply gives the matte from the coverage and the alpha of the input, and carry says which channels hold the matte

parameters.maps_to: Which channels hold the matte: alpha (colour passes), luma (the three colour channels, alpha at full scale) or all four.
How the coverage meets the alpha of the input frame: it replaces it, multiplies it or the larger of the two is kept.
How the coverage of a pixel is found: the exact area, one sample at the pixel centre, or the fraction of a sample pattern (Config::method).
The size of the sample pattern: samples-grid takes samples by samples points per pixel, samples-rotated takes samples points.
Which winding numbers count as inside (Config::fill).
Pixel i has its centre at coordinate i + centre (Config::centre).
Whether row 0 of the frame is at the smallest y, or at the largest (Config::y_down).
How the coverages of several polygons become one plane, in file order (Config::combine).
Whether a coverage value stays a double or is rounded to single precision after each step (Config::precision).
0 leaves coordinates as they are; n from 1 to 30 rounds every coordinate to a multiple of 2^-n first (Config::snap_bits).
Whether the rasteriser converts the coverage to a code of the depth of the stream (Config::quantise).
The factor from coverage 1 to a code: the largest value of the depth, or that value plus one; read when quantise is on (Quantise::scale).
How a scaled coverage becomes a whole code; read when quantise is on (Quantise::rounding).
Added to the x of every point before the rasteriser runs, in pixels; may be keyed.
Added to the y of every point before the rasteriser runs, in pixels; may be keyed.

layers.holds: The polygons to rasterise: rings of points in pixels of the frame. Without it nothing is covered.
A key file with a value per frame for offset_x and offset_y.

geometry: preserve: the output has the width, height, depth, rate and frame count of the input; --describe answers the request, or refuses what apply refuses before the first frame, and opens no layer
sample_rule: with quantise=on the rasteriser gives codes of the depth of the stream and a code is its value divided by full scale; with quantise=off, and at depth 32, the coverage is rounded to f32; apply gives the matte from the coverage and the alpha of the input in f32; on the way out a sample x of depth 8 or 16 is floor(clamp(x, 0, 1) * max + 0.5), and depth 32 is not clamped
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame, broken_pipe or stage_failed

exit_codes_table.means: every input frame was written; an empty input is zero frames; --describe printed its answer
stage_failed: a write failed for a reason other than a closed pipe, or the rasteriser failed on a frame; no scenario here reaches it
usage: a bad or missing option, a parameter or a layer given twice, a layer with an empty path

unsupported: a depth, a parameter, a layer or a value the stage does not take, a frame above the limits of the rasteriser, a number of the shape file above 1e9 in absolute value, a key for a parameter that is not keyed
bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe: a layer file that cannot be read or does not follow its form, an input that ends inside a frame, a frame count other than --frames, a reader that went away
